title: Why Do We Get GOOSEBUMPS? 😱
description:
A scary movie, a cold breeze, a great song... and your arm turns into plucked goose skin. Each hair on your arm has its own tiny muscle. When you're scared or cold, your nerves fire them all at once: the hair stands up, and the skin around it bunches into a bump. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

For furry animals it's a brilliant trick: fluffed-up fur traps warm air and makes a scared cat look huge. We lost the fur but kept the reflex. Music can set it off too: scientists think a big emotional moment trips the same alarm system. And a few people can raise goosebumps on command (a 2018 study tested 32 of them).
